(P. Longobardi, M. Maj, A. H. Rhemtulla). Let w = w(x1 , . . . , xn ) be a group
word in n variables x1 , . . . , xn , and V (w) the variety of groups defined by the law
w = 1. Let V (w∗ ) (respectively, V (w# )) be the class of all groups G in which for
every n infinite subsets S1 , . . . , Sn there exist si ∈ Si such that w(s1 , . . . , sn ) = 1
(respectively, ⟨s1 , . . . , sn ⟩ ∈ V (w)).
    a) Is there some word w and an infinite group G such that G ∈ V (w# ) but
G∈ / V (w)?
    b) Is there some word w and an infinite group G such that G ∈ V (w∗ ) but
G∈ / V (w# )?
    The answer to both of these questions is likely to be “yes”. It is known that in a)
w cannot be any of several words such as xn1 , [x1 , . . . , xn ], [x1 , x2 ]2 , (x1 x2 )3 x−3 −3
